title: homelab-evidence-mcp configuration
description: Use these rules for editor validation. The binary uses more validation rules. Always run this command: homelab-evidence-mcp --config path --validate

default_window.description: Use a Go duration, for example 1h.

max_log_lines.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 100.

max_evidence_items.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 200.

max_incident_response_bytes.description: Set the compact incident response budget. The default is 262144 and the maximum is 4194304.

max_log_line_bytes.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 2048 bytes.

max_body_bytes.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 2 MiB. The maximum is 8 MiB.

evidence_cache_ttl.description: Set the local cache TTL for get_evidence.

evidence_cache_max.description: A value of 0 deactivates the get_evidence cache.

evidence_cache_max_bytes.description: Set the serialized evidence payload budget for get_evidence. The default is 8 MiB and the maximum is 64 MiB. This value is not exact process memory.

source_cache_ttl.description: The source response cache keeps the same GET responses for a short time. The default is 15s. A value of 0 deactivates this cache. The source or collection time supplies the evidence timestamp.

max_tool_calls_per_minute.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 120.

max_source_requests_per_minute.description: Bound one source instance to this many requests in a sliding minute. A value of 0 uses 100. Healthchecks recommends at most 100.

max_concurrent_tools.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 8.

file.description: Set the optional path for the rotating JSONL audit log. The binary sets mode 0600 on Unix. On Windows, use a user-only ACL. The binary does not examine Windows ACLs.

max_bytes.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 10 MiB.

max_files.description: A value of 0 uses the default of 3.

tls.description: The TLS configuration can include an optional CA bundle. TLS certificate verification is always active.

ca_file.description: The PEM file contains CA certificates that the client adds to the system trust store.

base_url.description: Use an absolute http(s) URL. The client keeps path prefixes. It does not accept userinfo, query strings, or fragments.

api_version.description: Use only for a docker source. Add an explicit Engine API prefix such as v1.56 to read routes. Do not also put a version in base_url.

ca_file.description: Add extra CA trust for this source only. It replaces the global tls.ca_file for this source. TLS hostname verification stays active.

items.description: Use an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR. Every dial must resolve to an address in one of these networks.

allowed_cidrs.description: Optional per-source dial-time address policy. It mitigates DNS rebinding and limits a source to approved networks. TLS hostname verification stays active.

token_file.description: Use a regular file with a maximum size of 4 KiB. On Unix, let only the owner access the file. Use mode 0600. The binary does not accept files that a group or other users can access. On Windows, use a user-only ACL. The binary does not examine Windows ACLs.

token_header.description: Use X-Api-Key by default for Healthchecks. Use Authorization for other sources.

headers.description: Use static headers without secrets. Do not use authentication-related names or reserved headers.

allOf.description: Do not set both token_env and token_file.

selector.description: Use a simple LogQL selector with optional |= or |~ filters. The binary validates the syntax.

check_name.description: Match one check by name or slug. More than one match is an ambiguous_binding error. Prefer check_unique_key or check_uuid for one check.

check_unique_key.description: Use the unique_key from a read-only Healthchecks API key. Do not combine it with check_uuid.

history_mode.description: Use snapshot for current state only. Use transitions to read dated up/down history in windowed failed_crons and incident_context.
